claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and does not live with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Claimant contributes £26.05/week towards child's upkeep (>= £26.05) and no other claimaint has priority
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand your situation. 

**First, let me ask about the child (or children) you're applying for:**

Do you have a child or young person you're responsible for? If yes, could you tell me:
1. Their name (or names if you have multiple children)
2. Their age (or ages)

This will help me determine which eligibility path applies to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. His name is Alex and he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old.

Since Alex is under 16 years old, he falls into the automatic qualification age category. Let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now, the next question:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Given that Alex is only 8 years old, I would expect he's not working at all, but I need to confirm this to continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work at all. He's only 8, so he's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, that makes sense! Since Alex is 8 years old and not working, let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

This means benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit that would be claimed in his own name (not your benefits - his own). 

For an 8-year-old in primary school, this would be very unusual, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 8-year-old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next check:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

Again, for an 8-year-old in primary school, this would not apply, but I need to confirm he's not in any apprenticeship program.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not. He's only 8 and still in primary school, so no apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship, let me move to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient financial resources
6. You have pre-settled status as a student with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since you normally live in the UK (in Manchester), you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You qualify if ANY of the following applies:

1. **You live with Alex** (this is the most common situation)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep (paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care - food, clothes, housing, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Do any of these apply to you? For example, does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep - things like clothes, school supplies, that sort of thing.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To determine if your contributions meet the responsibility requirement, I need to understand a bit more:

**Do you pay at least the same amount as Child Benefit would be (or provide equivalent support in kind) towards Alex's care?**

Let me get the current Child Benefit rate for you to compare:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see that the exact current payment rates aren't specified in my reference materials, but as of recent rates, Child Benefit is approximately **£25.60 per week for the eldest (or only) child**.

So the question is: **Do your contributions for Alex (clothes, school supplies, and other support) add up to at least £25.60 per week** (which would be around £110 per month)?

This can include:
- Money you give directly
- Items you buy like clothes, school supplies, food
- Other contributions towards his care

Do your contributions meet or exceed this amount?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute more than that. I give about £26 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since you contribute at least £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which meets the responsibility requirement, let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about other potential claimants.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else who might be claiming for him

If someone else is claiming, have they agreed to transfer the claim to you, or is there a dispute about who should claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation to see if any special rules apply.

**Which of the following best describes Alex's current situation?**

1. Alex is in hospital
2. Alex is in local authority care
3. Alex is fostered
4. None of the above - Alex is living normally (at home with family)

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: None of those apply - Alex is living normally with family.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Since Alex is living normally, let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the local council paying for Alex's living costs or care? (If the council is not paying anything towards Alex's costs, the answer would be "yes" to this question.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's costs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Based on all the information you've provided, let me provide you with the eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Good News - You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!

Based on the assessment, **you meet all the eligibility requirements** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

✅ **Alex qualifies** - He's 8 years old (under 16), not working, not receiving benefits in his own right, and not in an apprenticeship

✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK (Manchester)

✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - You contribute £26 per week towards his upkeep, which meets the responsibility requirement

✅ **No other claimant** - No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

✅ **No council support** - The local council is not paying for Alex's care

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware**: If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, the High Income Child Benefit Charge may apply (this is a tax charge, but doesn't affect your eligibility)
5. **Payments**: Child Benefit is typically paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### Apply Here:
📋 **https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim**

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or the application process?
